description: Composite AES (Auger electron spectroscopy) sputter depth-profile figure, two stacked parts, both built from line+symbol plots of elemental concentration (at.%, y-axis) against sputtering time (min, x-axis 0-12); no micrographs, scale bars or maps are present despite the caption wording "AES images". (a) contains four vertically stacked panels, each annotated in its top-left corner with one sample - S0, S950, S1050, S1150 - sharing a legend in the top panel for O (star), Fe (circle), Al (triangle) and Mn (square), with visible error bars on the Mn points; y-axis spans 0-80 at.% in all four. (b) re-plots the same data as four stacked panels labelled by element (O, Fe, Al, Mn from top to bottom; Mn axis 0-20, others 0-80), each comparing S0 (red star), S950 (green hexagon), S1050 (blue triangle) and S1150 (magenta square). In every panel O begins near 60-65 at.% and decays while Fe rises from roughly 10-20 to 60-65 at.%; a vertical dashed line annotated with the film thickness (16.2±0.8 nm, 25.2±1.2 nm, 21.6±1 nm, 18±0.9 nm for S0, S950, S1050, S1150) marks where O falls to half its maximum. S0 loses O earliest and has the lowest Al level (~18 at.% at the surface), while S950 retains O and Al longest and forms the thickest, most Al-rich film.

observations.observation: Panel (a) consists of four stacked line plots, each labelled in the top-left with a sample name: S0, S950, S1050, S1150.
Both panels use y-axis 'Concentration (at.%)' (0-80 in all panels except the Mn panel of (b), which is 0-20) and x-axis 'Sputtering time (min)' spanning 0-12.

The legend of (a) assigns O to star markers, Fe to circles, Al to triangles and Mn to squares; the legend of (b) assigns S0 to red stars, S950 to green hexagons, S1050 to blue triangles and S1150 to magenta squares.
Four printed thickness annotations accompany vertical dashed lines: 16.2±0.8 nm, 25.2±1.2 nm, 21.6±1 nm and 18±0.9 nm, in the S0, S950, S1050 and S1150 panels respectively.

In every panel the O concentration starts near 60-65 at.% at zero sputtering time and decreases with depth while the Fe concentration rises to roughly 60-65 at.%, i.e. an oxygen-enriched surface film over the substrate composition.
The surface Al concentration in panel (a) is lowest in S0 (about 18 at.%) and highest in S950 (about 33 at.%), with S1050 and S1150 intermediate (~29-32 at.%).
In panel (b) the O curve of S0 drops earliest (already falling before ~3 min) whereas the S950 O curve stays near 60 at.% until roughly 5 min, indicating the deepest oxide film for S950.

The caption describes (a) as the 'comparison between different samples' and (b) as the 'comparison between different elements', but in the pixels (a) is grouped by sample and (b) is grouped by element - the caption wording and the panel grouping do not line up.
The caption calls these 'AES images of the oxide film of the LDSs', whereas the panels themselves are quantitative concentration-versus-sputtering-time line plots, not images or elemental maps.
The citing text states the oxide film thickness of S0 is approximately 16.2 ± 0.8 nm and of S950 25.2 ± 1.2 nm, matching the numbers printed on the panels.
The citing text states the S1050 and S1150 oxide films are 21.6 ± 1 nm and 18 ± 0.9 nm thick respectively, matching the annotations in panel (a).

The citing text states the S0 oxide film consists mainly of Fe, Al and O with Fe and Al in roughly comparable amounts, while the S950 film is predominantly uniformly distributed Al oxide with low Fe and Mn - consistent with the near-equal surface Fe/Al levels in the S0 panel and the high Al plateau of S950.

The citing text attributes the lowest Al content of the S0 oxide film to retained κ-carbide in the untreated S0 sample limiting Al solid solubility; this mechanism is not visible in the figure itself.
The citing text concludes that both oxide film thickness and Al content tend to decrease with increasing grain size, so that S950 forms a uniform, dense, thick Al-rich film.

subfigures.description: Four stacked concentration vs sputtering time plots, one per sample (S0, S950, S1050, S1150), y = Concentration (at.%) 0-80, x = Sputtering time (min) 0-12; shared legend O (star), Fe (circle), Al (triangle), Mn (square). Each panel carries a vertical dashed line annotated with an oxide-film thickness: 16.2±0.8 nm (S0), 25.2±1.2 nm (S950), 21.6±1 nm (S1050), 18±0.9 nm (S1150). O falls and Fe rises with depth in all samples; Al is ~18 at.% at the surface of S0 but ~30-34 at.% in the solution-treated samples.

Four stacked panels labelled with the element analysed (O, Fe, Al, Mn top to bottom), y = Concentration (at.%), x = Sputtering time (min) 0-12 (Mn panel y = 0-20), each overlaying the four samples S0 (red star), S950 (green hexagon), S1050 (blue triangle), S1150 (magenta square). Shows that S0's O decreases earliest, that S950 keeps O and Al high to the greatest sputtering time, and that S0 has the lowest surface Al (~18 at.%). Statistically scattered points carry error bars.

unreadable_items: error-bar magnitudes are not printed on any panel (only symbol size of the error bars is visible)
panel (b) Mn curves overlap and individual point values cannot be read exactly; only trends are legible
